hyperedges.label: The four-rung scaffolding system, from principle to pixel

nodes.label: Per-activity brain model routing
nodes.rationale: Claude Sonnet 5 answers realtime turns and designs scenes; Claude Opus 5 does post-session work (learner memory, drill authoring). Anthropic is the default because coaching quality is the product. A Groq/Llama 3.3 free-tier fallback exists for plumbing work with visibly weaker coaching.

nodes.label: Four-rung scaffolding ladder
nodes.rationale: Never let the learner be stuck: support is present by default and withdrawn as they improve, not absent and granted on request. Implemented once as a state machine so the app and the tutor agent run the same pedagogy.

nodes.label: Chrome is plain English, French only where it is content
nodes.rationale: Sentence case on buttons; the caps look survives only in the micro-label style. French appears exactly where it is content (tutor lines, lesson text, glosses, topic chips, review fronts) plus the single flourish 'Bonjour, {name}' on Home, which is lesson-one vocabulary. The old FRENCH / ENGLISH paired furniture is retired. No em dashes where a learner reads; short plain sentences — enforced for core content by packages/core/src/copy.test.ts.
nodes.norm_label: chrome is plain english, french only where it is content

nodes.label: No number and no scolding mid-session
nodes.rationale: Two hard rules held from the enamel era: no mid-session message contains a number (end cards may count, a session may not score), and no mid-session message scolds — no 'wrong', 'bad', 'failed', 'incorrect'. A rescue reads 'Let's take that one together.'
nodes.norm_label: no number and no scolding mid-session

nodes.label: Never stranded and never scolded
nodes.rationale: No mid-session scores, no 'wrong', no commenting on hesitation. The tutor steps in and carries the conversation the way a good human tutor does. Derived from confirmed research, not preference.

nodes.label: Live when reachable, Demo fallback otherwise
nodes.rationale: Home shows Live when the token server is reachable and the session runs over LiveKit; otherwise a small Demo label and automatic fallback to the mock pipeline. Degradation is visible but never a dead end.
nodes.norm_label: live when reachable, demo fallback otherwise

nodes.label: Accounts work without Supabase via a local on-device store
nodes.rationale: With no Supabase configured, accounts live in a local on-device store — any email works and the Google button signs into a dev account instantly. Real accounts are one env file away (EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / ANON_KEY); setting SUPABASE_URL on the token server makes it verify users instead of trusting the client.
nodes.norm_label: accounts work without supabase via a local on-device store

nodes.label: Mock speech pipeline runs the full loop with no API keys
nodes.rationale: The mock pipeline produces a genuine anglophone error pattern so ladder, rescue, scoring and drill selection are real without credentials. The demo instruction is to say nothing for four seconds: the tutor steps in, drops a rung, offers the line, and never comments on the pause.
nodes.norm_label: mock speech pipeline runs the full loop with no api keys

nodes.label: Learner-accented French breaks ordinary STT
nodes.rationale: Named as the hardest technical risk in the build: the transcription layer must survive genuinely bad beginner audio, not clean native speech.

nodes.label: Cascaded STT to LLM to TTS voice pipeline
nodes.rationale: Realtime voice via LiveKit Agents, deliberately cascaded rather than a speech-to-speech model: cost and French-quality control both demand the cascade. Latency target under 800ms from end-of-learner-speech to first tutor audio.
nodes.norm_label: cascaded stt to llm to tts voice pipeline

nodes.label: Metered minutes enforced from v1
nodes.rationale: Trial is a finite 30 minutes total, not a daily allowance. Paid tiers around $19/180min and $39/450min. Unlimited pricing is rejected on modelled unit economics, because premium French TTS voices are the dominant cost line and also the quality signal a beginner feels first.

nodes.label: Metering enforced at token issuance
nodes.rationale: An out-of-minutes learner gets a 402 and the out-of-minutes screen, and consumed seconds are debited by the agent when the room closes — so killing the app does not dodge the meter. Enforcement sits server-side because the client cannot be trusted with the balance.

nodes.label: Risk 2: cost per session
nodes.source_location: The two things to check before building further
nodes.rationale: Premium voice is roughly 60% of the per-minute cost. The cost model is instrumented and tested but must be reconciled against real vendor bills in week one, not month three.

nodes.label: Risk 1: STT on real learner French
nodes.source_location: The two things to check before building further
nodes.rationale: Issen ran four transcription models in parallel and still shipped complaints. Measure word error rate on genuinely bad beginner audio — not your own — before trusting any pronunciation output.
nodes.norm_label: risk 1: stt on real learner french

nodes.label: Self-hosted open-source LiveKit, the $0 stack
nodes.rationale: Transport is LiveKit built from source into ~/.local/bin/livekit-server so no LiveKit Cloud account is needed; both .env files point at ws://localhost:7880 with dev credentials that are localhost-only and must never be exposed.

nodes.label: Sentence-level TTS warm cache
nodes.rationale: Every scripted lesson line is synthesized once and saved to disk, after which lesson audio replays at no cost and with no synthesis delay; only free-form tutor replies use live synthesis. Lines are cached one sentence at a time to match how the voice pipeline requests them at runtime — a whole-line cache entry would never be hit.

nodes.label: Words-right and sounds-right are separate questions
nodes.rationale: Lexical/grammatical correctness and pronunciation accuracy are never collapsed into one verdict, so a learner who chose the right words but mangled a vowel is not told they were simply wrong.
nodes.norm_label: words-right and sounds-right are separate questions

nodes.label: Inline SVG illustration style contract
nodes.rationale: Authored inline SVG, one contract stated in the file header: ink stroke 2.2 round-capped, fill=none except tiny solid accents (a tenth of a scene at most), stipple-dot shading, quirky proportions, viewBox 200x150, no second colour so the paper shows through. Eight scenes: cafe hero, name tag, birthday cake, suitcase, winged clock, clinking speech bubbles, sprouting word cards, postcard. Authored rather than sourced so the whole set stays on one pen and ships with no asset pipeline.

nodes.label: fitDisplay length-stepped French line
nodes.rationale: frenchLg steps 28 -> 24 -> 20 by string length so the line to say always fits without the learner scrolling or squinting mid-utterance.

nodes.label: Fraunces speaks, DM Sans is furniture
nodes.rationale: Fraunces (72pt optical statics) carries anything with a voice — headlines, big stats, and every French line the learner reads, always sentence case, never caps. DM Sans is chrome. Both OFL and committed to assets/fonts/ with licences so the build has no font-CDN dependency. IPA uses DM Sans Medium 14 as real notation, not mono-as-costume.
nodes.norm_label: fraunces speaks, dm sans is furniture

nodes.label: French only, in depth
nodes.rationale: A hand-built French phoneme inventory weighted for English-L1 error patterns, mapped to minimal-pair drills. Issen's founders publicly conceded quality collapses in untested languages, so depth in one language beats breadth across fifty — and a competitor cannot copy it without changing shape.

nodes.label: Say one thing, not everything
nodes.rationale: The end of a session names a single sound to work on. Eleven red bars teaches a beginner they are bad at French.

nodes.label: A real spoken exchange inside one five-minute session
nodes.rationale: Success is a beginner completing a first session without getting stuck or asking a human for help, and returning because they can feel and see progress.
nodes.norm_label: a real spoken exchange inside one five-minute session

nodes.label: No streak guilt
nodes.rationale: Streaks are a guilt mechanic implicated in intermediate-plateau churn. Progress is framed forward ('three sounds from unlocking the cafe scenario'), never as a loss to protect. Competence over compulsion: retention comes from visible improvement, not streak anxiety.

nodes.label: Absolute-beginner audience (CEFR A0-A2)
nodes.rationale: English-speaking adults with no French vocabulary who practise alone on a phone in short sessions. The defining trait: they cannot compose a French sentence unaided, so an open question makes them freeze — and every existing AI tutor reads that freeze as 'still thinking' and waits.

nodes.label: Parle (working name)
nodes.rationale: An AI French speaking tutor for English-speaking absolute beginners. Name is explicitly a placeholder the user may replace, not confirmed final.

nodes.label: Expo + TypeScript npm-workspaces monorepo
nodes.rationale: One Expo/React Native codebase ships to iOS first, then Android, then web, with one shared design language rather than per-OS adaptive design. Shared pure-TS logic lives in packages/core; the tutor runs as a LiveKit Agents worker in services/tutor-agent.

nodes.label: Trustworthy pronunciation needs a reference text
nodes.rationale: Accuracy scoring requires a known reference text. Speak and Issen both lead with open-ended conversation, which is why their users call the speech recognition 'too forgiving'. Beginners spend most of a session on scripted and cued turns, so scoring is reliable precisely where this audience lives. This constraint shapes the whole scaffolding design; free conversation yields fluency signals only.
nodes.norm_label: trustworthy pronunciation needs a reference text

nodes.label: The alignment thesis
nodes.rationale: Beginners spend most of a session on scripted turns, so the audience nobody serves well is the exact audience where trustworthy pronunciation scoring is possible. Duolingo teaches recognition not speech; Speak and Issen strand beginners and score too forgivingly. That alignment is the whole thesis.

nodes.label: A missing score is never an invented penalty
nodes.rationale: scoreUtterance returns nothing without audio or a SpeechAce key, and every layer treats a missing score as 'don't invent a penalty' — the drill falls back to honest self-report rather than guessing the learner did badly.
nodes.norm_label: a missing score is never an invented penalty

nodes.label: packages/core is deliberately platform-free
nodes.rationale: No network, no mic, no keys in packages/core, so the app and the tutor agent run the same tested pedagogy. There is one implementation of the ladder, not two.

nodes.label: Repo path contains a space
nodes.rationale: The repo lives at a path containing a space ('Language Speaker'). Web and EAS cloud builds handle it, but local native tooling historically does not; renaming to a space-free directory before the first local iOS build is cheap insurance.

nodes.label: SpeakCircle, the one microphone
nodes.rationale: One 108pt circle reused by every speaking surface: red-ringed when waiting, red-filled when live (the app's only shadow), hairline-muted when the tutor holds the floor. A single microphone affordance means the learner never has to work out which control speaks.

nodes.label: Motion still has no design
nodes.rationale: There is no authored transition between rungs or pages. The support block changing shape is the product's most meaningful state change and deserves one orchestrated moment; it survived the restyle as the first thing to add next. App icon and splash are still enamel-era placeholders on paper-coloured ground.

nodes.label: One primary action per screen
nodes.rationale: Exactly one solid ink PillButton (52pt) per screen; seconds are OutlineButton or GhostButton. Carried over from the enamel era unchanged because it is behaviour rather than surface. Cards are flat with a single hairline rule, no shadows anywhere except the live microphone glow.

nodes.label: Signal colours kept out of the rung set
nodes.rationale: live #FF4B3E, good #1E8A5B, correspondance #B4008A are deliberately excluded from the rung palette so a transient state never reads as a support rung. Both greens/magentas were darkened from the enamel era to hold contrast on white cards.
nodes.norm_label: signal colours kept out of the rung set

nodes.label: Support colours cool as help is withdrawn
nodes.source_location: Support colours still cool as help is withdrawn
nodes.rationale: Rung 1 Echo #FFCD00, 2 Cued #FF7E2E, 3 Prompted #6EC4E8, 4 Free plain ink #1A141E. The temperature drop is the learner's visible evidence that scaffolding is being removed; rung 4 has no colour left because there is no line left to follow. Survived the restyle unchanged because it is behaviour, not surface.
nodes.norm_label: support colours cool as help is withdrawn

nodes.label: Gate, onboarding, Home with Speak and Learn tabs
nodes.rationale: Sign-in gate -> four onboarding pages -> Home with two tabs. Speak holds the conversation and the guided lesson that unlocks it, with 'Unable to speak right now?' opening the same tutor in text mode. Learn holds tutor-picked practice. Screens remain a hand-rolled discriminated union in App.tsx — still no navigation library.
nodes.norm_label: gate, onboarding, home with speak and learn tabs

nodes.label: Read the exact versioned Expo docs before writing code
nodes.rationale: Standing instruction for agents working in apps/mobile: Expo has changed, so read the exact versioned docs for v57.0.0 before writing any code rather than relying on remembered APIs.
nodes.norm_label: read the exact versioned expo docs before writing code

nodes.label: 460pt centred web column
nodes.rationale: On web the app is a 460pt centred column — a phone app that also runs in a browser, not a stretched web page. Keeps one layout across iOS, Android and web instead of a responsive second design.

nodes.label: Paper colour token set
nodes.rationale: Light and committed to one paper: ground #F3E8F3, groundDeep #EAD9EA, card #FFFFFF, ink #1A141E (near-black with a whisper of violet), inkSoft, inkFaint, line, lineOnCard, onInk #FFF9F2 (warm, never pure white on an ink control). One paper means no dark-mode fork to maintain.

nodes.label: Drill mode and the recognition-to-production ramp
nodes.rationale: Fill-blank, best-sentence, appropriate-reply, tap-translate, listen-type and repeat-this, with typo-tolerant grading and re-queue-until-correct, ramping from recognition to production over the review deck, plus a 'can't speak now' mic swap so a learner in public is never blocked.
nodes.norm_label: drill mode and the recognition-to-production ramp

nodes.label: Paper & Ink design world
nodes.rationale: A picture book for adults: pale lilac paper, warm black ink, hand-drawn line art, a serif that speaks and a sans that stays out of the way. Chosen because the product asks a nervous adult to speak out loud twice a day, and the surface that earns that is calm, friendly and professional. Replaces the earlier enamel-wayfinding / dark Metro-plaque-green system, which lives on at the repo baseline commit. Every value is read out of apps/mobile/src/theme.ts as shipped, not from intentions.

nodes.label: Everything spoken must also be readable
nodes.rationale: The learner may be in a quiet carriage, hard of hearing, or unsure what they heard. Speaking aloud in public is socially costly, so the product must never require the learner to speak loudly or repeatedly to progress. Touch targets sized for one-handed use while walking; text must survive OS dynamic type scaling.
nodes.norm_label: everything spoken must also be readable

nodes.label: Absent evidence must not be fabricated
nodes.rationale: No testimonials, learner counts, retention figures, App Store presence, press or funding exist for this product. Competitor figures in the plan are researched and sourced; our own numbers are zero and must stay zero in any copy.
nodes.norm_label: absent evidence must not be fabricated

nodes.label: The conversation upgrade
nodes.rationale: Sessions open on 'Alors, de quoi on parle aujourd'hui ?' with topic chips; a spoken or tapped topic runs the scenario builder with fixture scenes as fallback, never a failure. English answers get the French handed back and the beat re-invited; 'plus lent' makes the tutor slow and keeps it slow; corrections render as quote then better. After the recap an analyst extracts what it learned about the learner and authors tomorrow's drills from today's phrases. Text mode (sans micro) is the same brain with the voice pipeline dark.

nodes.label: The agent is authoritative over session state
nodes.rationale: The agent owns the ladder and lesson state; the app renders what it is sent over the LiveKit data channel using the shared protocol package. A single authority prevents client and agent disagreeing about which rung the learner is on.
nodes.norm_label: the agent is authoritative over session state
